description: Named cases for the full per-(rom, filename, slot) decision of the reference model: branch selection (newest head by updated_at), the three device_syncs branches, the corrupt-local guard, both identity routes (parity AND provenance), and the timestamp fall-through. Curated, not exhaustive — the input space is unbounded. Hash strings and timestamps are placeholders; only presence, equality, and relative order carry meaning. Timestamps always carry an explicit UTC offset so parsing is environment-independent.

vectors.name: no-server-saves-local-present
vectors.rationale: Nothing on the server side of the slot: a present local file is the only content — upload it as the first save.

vectors.name: no-server-saves-no-local
vectors.rationale: Neither side has anything for this file — nothing to sync.

vectors.name: entries-on-older-save-dont-count
vectors.rationale: This device is current on an OLDER save, but the decision branches on the NEWEST save's device_syncs only — no entry there, local absent, adopt the head.

vectors.name: unparseable-timestamp-loses
vectors.rationale: A save whose updated_at cannot be parsed never beats a parseable one, whatever the list order.

vectors.name: current-local-gone-recovery
vectors.rationale: The server still tracks this device's last upload but the local copy disappeared — download to recover the canonical content.

vectors.name: current-no-baseline-parity
vectors.rationale: Current on the head, local present without a baseline, but byte-identical to the head (parity — the only identity route without history): adopt it as the baseline so future runs can detect drift. Pure bookkeeping, no transfer.

vectors.name: current-no-baseline-different
vectors.rationale: Current on the head, local present without a baseline and NOT identical to the head: the differing hash is either an edit made since or local hashing drifting from the server's scheme, and without a baseline nothing tells which. Adopting it would hide an edit from every later run, and uploading it is a guess — unknown provenance, the user decides.

vectors.name: current-no-baseline-head-hash-unknown
vectors.rationale: Current on the head, local present without a baseline, and the head states no content_hash: identity cannot be proven, and unknown never proves anything — conflict, not an adoption.

vectors.name: current-no-baseline-local-hash-unknown
vectors.rationale: Current on the head, local present without a baseline, but the local hash could not be computed: identity cannot be proven — conflict, not an adoption.

vectors.name: current-unchanged
vectors.rationale: Current on the head and local matches the recorded baseline — in sync, nothing to do.

vectors.name: current-diverged-uploads
vectors.rationale: Current on the head and local diverged from the baseline: an offline edit. Push it (overwrite=false — a stale-current race turns into a 409, resolved by the ladder).

vectors.name: current-diverged-shrunken
vectors.rationale: Local diverged AND shrank below half its recorded size — a truncated/corrupt write, not a plausible edit. Never auto-upload it; the user decides.

vectors.name: current-diverged-zero-byte
vectors.rationale: A 0-byte local is never a plausible edit, even without a recorded size — the corrupt-local guard fires unconditionally on empty files.

vectors.name: current-diverged-fill-dropped
vectors.rationale: The save recorded at the last sync held fill only (content size 0): mGBA's 131072 bytes of 0xFF before the game first reads its save. The local file is now the real 32768-byte save. Both sides state a content size, so the guard compares those, and content grown from nothing is no shrink, although the raw size fell below half.

vectors.name: current-diverged-blank-save
vectors.rationale: Same raw size as at the last sync, but the local file is fill only (content size 0) where the recorded content was larger: an emulator that failed to load the save and wrote a blank one of full size back. The raw size cannot see it; the content comparison does. Never auto-upload it.

vectors.name: current-diverged-content-shrunken
vectors.rationale: Same raw size as at the last sync, but the content shrank below half of what was recorded, the rest of the file now fill. A real shrink behind trailing fill is still a shrink.

vectors.name: current-diverged-content-shrink-within-half
vectors.rationale: The raw size fell below half of the recorded one, the content did not (24576 to 16384 bytes): what the file lost beyond that was fill. Both sides state a content size, so the content comparison decides, and a shrink within half is a plausible edit.

vectors.name: current-diverged-content-size-local-only
vectors.rationale: The local file states a content size, the record of the last sync does not (it was recorded without one). With either side absent the raw-size rule stands: 32768 is below half of 131072. An absent recorded content size is unknown, not 0.

vectors.name: current-diverged-content-size-recorded-only
vectors.rationale: The record of the last sync states a content size, the local file does not. With either side absent the raw-size rule stands: 1024 is below half of 8192. The local raw size does not stand in for its content size.

vectors.name: current-diverged-zero-byte-content-size
vectors.rationale: A 0-byte local file is refused on its raw size, even where both sides state a content size and the comparison alone would let it through (no content then, none now).

vectors.name: current-diverged-fill-only-still-no-content
vectors.rationale: The local file is fill only (content size 0), and so was the save recorded at the last sync. A content size of 0 is not refused outright: it goes through the comparison, and nothing is below half of no content.

vectors.name: current-diverged-content-size-without-raw-size
vectors.rationale: The local file states a content size but no raw size. Both sides state a content size, so those are compared without the raw size: 1024 is below half of 8192.

vectors.name: current-diverged-fixed-size-truncated
vectors.rationale: A save whose size the format fixes, 32768 bytes at the last sync, is now 20480 bytes, its content cut with it. That is within half of what was recorded, so the half rule lets it through. A fixed-size file never legitimately loses content; it can get shorter only by dropping trailing fill. Its raw size is below the 32768 bytes of content recorded at the last sync, so it is a truncated write. Never auto-upload it.

vectors.name: current-diverged-size-not-fixed-truncated
vectors.rationale: The same shortening as current-diverged-fixed-size-truncated, but the caller states that the size is not fixed: the file may legitimately get shorter. Only the half rule applies, and 20480 is not below half of 32768.

vectors.name: current-diverged-size-fixed-unknown-truncated
vectors.rationale: The same shortening as current-diverged-fixed-size-truncated, but the caller does not know whether the size is fixed and leaves size_fixed out. Unknown is not fixed: only the half rule applies, and 20480 is not below half of 32768.

vectors.name: current-diverged-fixed-size-fill-dropped
vectors.rationale: current-diverged-fill-dropped on a file stated fixed: mGBA's 131072 bytes of 0xFF, recorded with content size 0, give way to the real 32768-byte save. The fixed rule compares the raw size with the content recorded at the last sync, and 32768 is not below 0: what the file lost was fill.

vectors.name: current-diverged-fixed-size-trailing-fill-dropped
vectors.rationale: A fixed-size file went from 32768 to 20480 bytes, but the content recorded at the last sync was 16384 bytes and the raw size is not below it: what the file lost was trailing fill. The fixed rule compares against the recorded content, not the recorded raw size, so a shortening that drops only fill loses nothing and does not trip it.

vectors.name: current-diverged-fixed-size-no-content-recorded
vectors.rationale: The record of the last sync holds no content size, so the fixed rule compares against the recorded raw size: 30000 is below 32768. The half rule alone would let it through.

vectors.name: current-diverged-fixed-size-blank-save
vectors.rationale: current-diverged-blank-save on a file stated fixed: full size, fill only, where the recorded content was 24576 bytes. The fixed rule sees no shortening, since 32768 is not below 24576. The half rule on the content sizes applies to a fixed-size file all the same and refuses it: the fixed rule comes in addition, so a fixed-size file is never guarded more weakly than one whose size can change.

vectors.name: current-diverged-fixed-size-raw-size-unknown
vectors.rationale: The file is stated fixed, but its raw size could not be read. The fixed rule has nothing to compare and does not fire; an unknown size is not 0. Both sides state a content size, so the half rule compares those, and 20480 is not below half of 32768.

vectors.name: current-diverged-fixed-size-unchanged-size
vectors.rationale: An ordinary edit of a fixed-size save: the size is what it was at the last sync. Not below is not shrunken, so it uploads.

vectors.name: current-hash-unknown
vectors.rationale: Current on the head with a baseline recorded, but the local hash could not be computed: without it drift from the baseline cannot be claimed — treat as in sync rather than guessing.

vectors.name: moved-past-local-gone
vectors.rationale: The head moved past this device and there is no local file to protect — adopt the head.

vectors.name: moved-past-no-baseline-parity
vectors.rationale: Device not current on the head (moved past, or on RomM never synced), local present without a baseline, but byte-identical to the head (parity — the only identity route without history): identical bytes never travel — adopt the local file as the baseline instead of downloading the same content again. The server still holds this device not current on the head, so the result asks for an acknowledgement.

vectors.name: moved-past-no-baseline-different
vectors.rationale: Head moved past, local present without a baseline and NOT identical to the head: unknown provenance colliding with a moved head — the user decides.

vectors.name: moved-past-unchanged
vectors.rationale: Head moved past, local unchanged since the baseline and not identical to the head: this device holds no un-synced work — download the head.

vectors.name: moved-past-unchanged-provenance
vectors.rationale: PROVENANCE route on a moved head: local unchanged since the baseline AND the stored server hash equals the head's content_hash — the head moved to the very content this device last synced, proven by two server-produced hashes even though the local hash differs from the head's. Identical bytes never travel — adopt, no download. The server still holds this device not current on the head, so the result asks for an acknowledgement.

vectors.name: moved-past-unchanged-parity
vectors.rationale: PARITY route on a moved head with the local file unchanged since its baseline: the stored server hash differs from the head's, but the local hash equals the head's content_hash directly. Identical bytes never travel — adopt, no download. The server still holds this device not current on the head, so the result asks for an acknowledgement.

vectors.name: moved-past-diverged-identical
vectors.rationale: Both sides moved independently but landed on the SAME bytes: nothing to reconcile and nothing to transfer — adopt the local file as the baseline. The server still holds this device not current on the head, so the result asks for an acknowledgement.

vectors.name: moved-past-diverged-different
vectors.rationale: Both sides moved independently to DIFFERENT content — the genuine two-sided conflict.

vectors.name: moved-past-hash-unknown
vectors.rationale: Head moved past and the local hash is unknown: drift cannot be proven, and the server copy is the safe read — download.

vectors.name: never-synced-local-gone
vectors.rationale: No entry for this device on the head and no local file — adopt the head.

vectors.name: never-synced-parity-dedup
vectors.rationale: Local content is byte-identical to a head that carries no entry for this device (parity route): adopt it as the baseline instead of POSTing a duplicate.

vectors.name: never-synced-provenance-dedup
vectors.rationale: PROVENANCE route: local unchanged since baseline AND the stored server hash equals the head's content_hash — identity proven by two server-produced hashes even though the local hash differs from the head's (a local-hashing scheme drift). Adopt as baseline, no duplicate POST.

vectors.name: never-synced-baseline-diverged
vectors.rationale: Local diverged from its baseline while the chosen head carries no entry for this device: both sides moved — conflict.

vectors.name: never-synced-no-baseline-mtime-newer-still-conflicts
vectors.rationale: No baseline, local hash known and NOT identical to a head with no entry for this device: unknown provenance — conflict, even though the local mtime is newer. mtime never rescues this case.

vectors.name: never-synced-unchanged-mtime-newer
vectors.rationale: Local provably unchanged since its baseline, no entry for this device on the head and not identical (stored hash differs): fall through to the timestamp comparison — local at-or-after the head uploads as a new save.

vectors.name: never-synced-unchanged-mtime-equal
vectors.rationale: Timestamp tie on the fall-through path counts as local-newer — upload (at-or-after, not strictly-after).

vectors.name: never-synced-unchanged-mtime-older
vectors.rationale: Local provably unchanged and older than a head with no entry for this device — adopt the head.

vectors.name: never-synced-hash-unknown-mtime-newer
vectors.rationale: Local hash unknown: identity and drift are both unprovable, so the timestamp fallback decides — local newer uploads.

vectors.name: never-synced-hash-unknown-mtime-older
vectors.rationale: Local hash unknown, local older than the head — the safe read wins: download.

vectors.name: never-synced-mtime-missing
vectors.rationale: On the timestamp fallback path a missing local mtime cannot prove local-newer — the server wins: download.

vectors.name: never-synced-head-timestamp-garbage
vectors.rationale: On the timestamp fallback path an unparseable head updated_at cannot prove local-newer either — download the known-good server copy rather than trust broken metadata.

vectors.name: never-synced-empty-hash-behaves-unknown
vectors.rationale: An empty-string local hash proves nothing (same as unknown): no identity, no provenance claim — the timestamp fallback decides.

vectors.name: missing-content-hash-dedup-gap
vectors.rationale: Known gap, pinned deliberately: the head carries no content_hash (older/migrated save), local is unchanged and mtime-newer — the dedup check cannot run and the fall-through POSTs what may be a byte-identical duplicate. Harmless (a new version, no overwrite), but documented.
